issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Objectification: Being looked at sexually
issues.explanation: For a male civilian-in-war-zone trauma profile, sexual objectification as a central trigger is not impossible, but in combination with the rest of the profile it lacks support from memory, threat, and appraisal items. The other items consistently describe war-related threat, distrust, flashbacks, and sensory trauma memory rather than sexualized threat, making this trigger hard to integrate into the same trauma presentation.

issues.item: Triggers: Visual (Water/Flooding): Water, flooding, or large bodies of water
issues.explanation: Water/flooding as a trigger is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the selected items. No memory, threat, or appraisal items reference water, drowning, environmental disaster, or any related theme. Given the otherwise interpersonal/war-threat profile, this trigger appears disconnected from the formulation.

issues.item: Visual (Water/Flooding): Water, flooding, or large bodies of water
issues.explanation: The trigger set is not well aligned with the rest of the profile or the indexed trauma type. For a civilian in a war zone, water/flooding and alcohol smell are hard to reconcile with the threat, memory, and appraisal items unless there is some specific unreported trauma context linking them. The rest of the profile centers on generalized danger, distrust, flashbacks, and sensory recall, but these two triggers imply a different situational pattern that is not otherwise represented.

The maladaptive strategy set is partly disconnected from the rest of the formulation. Drug use is plausible as a broad coping strategy, but excessive exercise and concealing clothing suggest body-focused avoidance or managing visibility/safety in a specific way that is not supported by the memory, threat, or appraisal items presented. Given the strong Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies and Threat → Maladaptive Strategies links, these strategies should plausibly follow from the reported triggers and threat beliefs, but these two items do not clearly do so.

vignette: Ravi, a 24-year-old South Asian diplomat, has been struggling since his traumatic experience in a war-torn region. The event that deeply shook him occurred when he was caught in an explosion while on assignment. Though physically unharmed, the emotional and psychological toll of that day has left lasting scars. Even now, Ravi cannot shake the feeling of vulnerability that haunts him. Any hint of alcohol or the sound of a sudden bang sends him spiraling back to that moment when everything felt out of control. The smell of alcohol often brings him back to the aftermath, where soldiers and civilians alike drank heavily in an attempt to cope with their own trauma. These triggers have led Ravi to adopt several maladaptive strategies. He has taken to using drugs as a means to numb his heightened emotions and intrusive memories. He also pushes himself to exercise excessively, hoping that physical exhaustion might provide some respite from the relentless thoughts about the event. Wearing concealing clothing helps him feel slightly more protected, but it does little to quell the constant fear. The sense of vulnerability is not just emotional; Ravi feels constantly threatened by his surroundings. Even when others tell him he is safe, he finds it impossible to believe them. He frequently experiences flashbacks where he feels as though the explosion is happening again. This only deepens his mistrust and makes every stranger approaching him feel like a potential threat. Ravi's memories of that day are vivid and detailed. He can clearly recall the smell of smoke and burning rubber, which often resurfaces when he encounters similar scents. The clarity of these memories has left Ravi struggling to find words to describe his experience, but they remain etched in his mind, a constant reminder of what he went through. The trauma has also led Ravi to question everything about himself and the world around him. He believes there is something inherently wrong with him that made him a target for such an event. This loss of faith extends beyond just himself; he no longer trusts people or life itself. The feeling of hopelessness weighs heavily on him, making it difficult to envision any future. These negative appraisals have further fueled his maladaptive behaviors and heightened sense of threat. His drug use has become a desperate attempt to escape the intrusive memories that plague him. Every time he exercises excessively, it is an effort to maintain control over something in his life that feels so out of reach. The cycle continues to tighten around Ravi. The more vivid his memories become, the greater his sense of threat grows. This leads to more frequent drug use and compulsive exercise as coping mechanisms. His loss of faith reinforces these behaviors, creating a self-reinforcing loop where each component feeds into the next. Despite his efforts to manage his symptoms, they have taken a toll on Ravi's personal and professional life. He has become increasingly isolated from his partner, and his work performance has suffered due to frequent absences and difficulty concentrating. The constant fear and flashbacks have made it nearly impossible for him to function normally in his role as a diplomat. What finally brought Ravi to seek help was the realization that he could no longer carry this burden alone. He is most afraid of never feeling safe again, of being trapped in a perpetual state of hypervigilance. At the same time, he hopes for a future where he can reclaim some sense of normalcy and trust in himself and others. Ravi's journey has been one of gradual deterioration, with each layer of trauma reinforcing the next. The complex interplay between his triggers, maladaptive strategies, perceptions of threat, memory intrusions, and negative appraisals forms a tight knot that he is only now beginning to unravel.
